```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("rvis-setup.R")
```

rvis does two things:

1. **Charts with one calling convention.** `rvisPlot()` draws interactive charts with about
   30 plotting packages (htmlwidgets like echarts4r, highcharter, plotly, apexcharter, visNetwork or
   DT), always with the same arguments: the data, the columns to show, and a list of settings.
   Changing the package that draws a chart is changing one word.
2. **Shiny dashboards from a configuration.** `rvisDashboard()` builds a complete shiny app from a
   YAML (or JSON) file or an R list naming its inputs, outputs, containers and layout, with the R code
   of its outputs. Clicks on chart items can be inputs of the dashboard.

This page takes you from installation to your first chart and your first dashboard, and shows
where to go next.

## Installation

rvis is installed from GitHub. It needs package
[rutils](https://github.com/genpack/rutils), also on GitHub, which is installed with it:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("genpack/rvis")
```

The plotting packages are **optional**: install the ones whose charts you want to use. Each chart
of the [chart guides](#where-next) names the package it needs. The packages on CRAN:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("echarts4r", "apexcharter", "highcharter", "plotly", "billboarder", "c3",
                   "dygraphs", "rAmCharts", "googleVis", "networkD3", "visNetwork", "DiagrammeR",
                   "DT", "rpivotTable", "leaflet"))
```

For dashboards, install shiny and shinydashboard (and, for the features that use them, shinyWidgets,
shinyBS, shinyjs, rintrojs, shinythemes, yaml and jsonlite):

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("shiny", "shinydashboard", "yaml", "shinyWidgets", "shinyBS", "shinyjs", "rintrojs", "shinythemes"))
```

A few plotters use packages which are only on GitHub, like rCharts
(`remotes::install_github("ramnathv/rCharts")`), D3plusR (`"paulofelipe/D3plusR"`), streamgraph
(`"hrbrmstr/streamgraph"`) or sankeytreeR (`"timelyportfolio/sankeytreeR"`). The
[plotter list](adding-plotters.html) shows every plotter with its package.

## Your first chart

`rvisPlot()` takes the chart `type`, the `plotter` (the package drawing it), the data `obj`, the
columns of the dimensions of the chart (here `x` and `y`) and a `config` list of settings:

```{r first-chart, eval=has_plotter("echarts4r")}
library(rvis)
deaths <- data.frame(age = rownames(VADeaths), VADeaths, check.names = FALSE)

rvisPlot(type = "bar", plotter = "echarts", obj = deaths,
         x = "age", y = list("Rural Male", "Urban Male"),
         config = list(title = "Death rates in Virginia (1940)", yAxis.label = "per 1000"))
```

Several series are given as a list of columns, like `y = list("Rural Male", "Urban Male")`. The same
call draws the chart with another package by changing `plotter`:

```{r same-chart, eval=has_plotter("apexcharter")}
rvisPlot(type = "bar", plotter = "apexcharter", obj = deaths,
         x = "age", y = list("Rural Male", "Urban Male"),
         config = list(title = "Death rates in Virginia (1940)", yAxis.label = "per 1000"))
```

The charts are htmlwidgets: they are shown in the RStudio viewer, in R Markdown and Quarto
documents, and in shiny apps (with the output and render functions of their package).

## Your first dashboard

A dashboard is a list of named **items**, inputs, outputs and containers, and a **layout** naming the
item that makes the page. Outputs have a **service**: the R code of their content, run again when an
input it uses changes. Save this as `hello.yml`:

```yaml
name: Hello rvis
layout: page
items:
  page:
    type: sidebarLayout
    title: Hello rvis!
    layout.side: [bins]
    layout.main: [hist]
  bins:
    type: sliderInput
    title: "Number of bins:"
    min: 1
    max: 50
    value: 30
  hist:
    type: plotOutput
    service: |
      x <- faithful$waiting
      hist(x, breaks = seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = input$bins + 1),
           col = "#75AADB", border = "white", main = "Waiting times")
```

and run it:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
runDashboard("hello.yml")
```

![The Hello rvis dashboard: a slider for the number of bins and a histogram of the waiting times of the Old Faithful geyser](figures/dash-hello.png){width=100%}

This example comes with rvis. 40 example dashboards do, from single features to complete apps:
`rvisDashboardExample()` lists them, and `runDashboard(rvisDashboardExample("hello"))` runs one.

```{r}
head(rvisDashboardExample()[, c("name", "group", "title")], 10)
```

Charts of rvis are dashboard outputs too, and any function of any package can be an item, written as
`package::function`:

```yaml
  chart:
    type: echarts4r::echarts4rOutput
    click.events: true      # clicks on the bars set input$chart_item_click
    service: rvisPlot("bar", "echarts", obj = mtcars, x = "cyl", y = "mpg")
```
